Residential B.S. Business Administration & Data Analysis — Interdisciplinary Business

A campus business route with a partial published outside map and 120-credit ledger. Build a feasible campus finish that includes major residency, prerequisites and the campus experience you want.

What makes this route worth exploring

  • Published outside equivalencies
  • Conditional named waivers
  • Major and total residency allocation
  • Semester-by-semester campus planning

What needs to be confirmed

  • Total residency, major residency and upper-level work require separate checks.
  • Named waivers award no credits and require replacement credits; a blanket GE waiver was not verified.
  • Residential restrictions, prerequisites and seasonal offerings can add terms.
  • Resolve the C versus C-minus transfer-grade discrepancy if it affects your inventory.
  • A standard 120-credit residential degree has a 75% outside-credit ceiling.
  • At least 25% of major requirements must be completed at Liberty, with program conditions; the linked model reserves its stated major minimum.
  • A waiver does not create earned credits or reduce the degree total.

Eligibility and your situation

  • Confirm campus admission, housing and applicable aid.
  • State your desired campus time and need for live classes.

A practical sequence

  1. Lock the 2026–27 award and request evaluation.
  2. Apply existing and approved outside credit in the mapped draft.
  3. Confirm each requested named waiver and replacement-credit placement.
  4. Reserve total/major residency and sequence prerequisite chains.
  5. Build semesters from actual residential offerings, housing and aid.
  6. Finish campus work, open selections and official graduation audit.

Your next useful actions

  • Open the mapped residential draft and enter existing learning.
  • Ask Liberty for written waiver and grade-policy decisions that affect you.
  • Request a semester-by-semester schedule before choosing a campus start.

doctorate planning

Online Doctor of Business Administration: specialization to confirm

A doctoral transfer-comparison family for an applicant with relevant graduate work. The exact specialization, credit-age rules and research obligations must agree before estimating savings.

What makes this route worth exploring

  • Graduate transfer evaluation
  • Specialization fit
  • Research and institutional milestone planning

What needs to be confirmed

  • The existing library links a graduate matrix, not a verified DBA course map.
  • Transfer must fit actual doctoral requirements, current age limits and footnotes.
  • A ceiling does not remove research or minimum institutional obligations.

Eligibility and your situation

  • Confirm prior-degree, GPA, experience and specialization entry rules.
  • Check recognition for intended faculty, professional or employment use.

A practical sequence

  1. Choose current specialization and catalog.
  2. Confirm admission and collect graduate transcripts/syllabi.
  3. Obtain course-level transfer decisions including all age limits and footnotes.
  4. Map remaining coursework and research.
  5. Schedule institutional terms, supervision, approvals and final research.
  6. Complete doctoral audit and conferral.

Your next useful actions

  • Request the specialization curriculum and doctoral handbook.
  • Ask for course-level evaluation of graduate work.
  • Obtain the complete remaining tuition and research-fee schedule.

Criminal Justice (B.S.) — General, On campus

General Criminal Justice degree with a source-linked course ledger. Unmapped requirements remain visible.

What makes this route worth exploring

  • Published school course equivalencies
  • Transfer-credit allocation
  • University and major residency

What needs to be confirmed

  • At least 30 credits must be earned through Liberty; degree and major residency are separate.
  • The degree requires 30 upper-level credits.
  • The plan uses the general Criminal Justice track; concentrations have different requirements.
